title: RBAC Overview
description: Learn how Azure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) limits what identities can do in Azure.

data.text: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is Azure's system for managing who can do what. Instead of giving everyone admin access, you assign roles that match exactly the permissions needed for a job.
RBAC has three main parts: the security principal (who), the role definition (what they can do), and the scope (where the permissions apply).

data.title: RBAC Components
items: Security Principal — user, group, service principal, or managed identity
Role Definition — a collection of permissions like Reader, Contributor, or Owner
Scope — management group, subscription, resource group, or single resource
Role Assignment — the link that ties a principal to a role at a scope

data.title: Assign RBAC Role with Azure CLI
data.content: Grant a service principal Contributor access to a resource group.
data.code: az role assignment create   --assignee "service-principal-object-id"   --role Contributor   --resource-group myResourceGroup

data.title: Best Practice
data.text: Follow the principle of least privilege. Give the minimum permissions needed. You can always grant more later.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RBAC controls access with roles, not individual permissions.
Scope limits where a role applies.
Use least privilege — start with Reader, add permissions only when needed.
